148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

2	name: project-git
3	description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
4	---
5	
6	Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.
7	
8	## The model
9	
10	- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
11	  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
12	  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
13	  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
14	  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
15	  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
16	  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
17	- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
18	  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
19	  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
20	- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
21	  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
22	  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
23	  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
24	  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
25	  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
26	  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.
27	
28	So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
29	Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).
30	
31	## Recording your work (committing)
32	
33	Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
34	`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
35	would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:
36	
37	```bash
38	# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
39	"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
40	"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
41	  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
42	
43	# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
44	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
45	    add path/to/File.lean
46	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
47	    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
48	    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
49	```
50	
51	Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
52	files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
53	anything staged in your way.
54	
55	- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
56	  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
57	  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
58	  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
59	  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
60	- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
61	  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
62	  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
63	  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
64	  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
65	  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
66	- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
67	  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
68	  named obligation open.
69	- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
70	  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
71	- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
72	  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
73	- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
74	  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
75	  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
76	- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
77	  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
78	  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
79	  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
80	  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
81	  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.
82	
83	Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
84	`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
85	make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:
86	
87	```bash
88	"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
89	```
90	
91	## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard
92	
93	Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
94	seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
95	then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
96	plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
97	The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
98	you did not ask for:
99	
100	- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
101	  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
102	  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
103	  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:
104	
105	  ```bash
106	  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
107	  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
108	  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
109	  ```
110	
111	- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
112	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.
113	
114	At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
115	since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
116	blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):
117	
118	```bash
119	"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
120	"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
121	```
122	
123	If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
124	working tree, commit once.
125	
126	## Reading history / a project's diff
127	
128	Run from the workspace root:
129	
130	```bash
131	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
132	
133	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
134	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
135	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
136	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
137	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
138	```
139	
140	Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
141	`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
142	run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:
143	
144	```bash
145	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
146	  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
147	```
148	
149	To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
150	the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
151	commit changed).
152	
153	## Caveats
154	
155	- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
156	  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
157	  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
158	  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
159	- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

11	/-!
12	# The target degree is a WINDOW, not the genus — and at `deg = g` the two chart conditions coincide
13	
14	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` proves that a class of degree **exactly** `g` on a
15	curve with `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` has an effective representative of degree `g`, and its
16	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` docstring carries a retraction that ends:
17	
18	> "**So what this lemma does is RELOCATE the hypothesis, not discharge it** — `Z` is an
19	> argument. […] Producing `Z` is a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open here."
20	
21	That retraction is **correct about `= g` and wrong about the obligation**, and this file
22	separates the two.  The arithmetic obstruction it records is real: `CurveDivisor.deg` is
23	weighted by residue degrees (`RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean`), so its image is `index · ℤ`, and on
24	a curve of index `3` and genus `1` there is no divisor of degree `1 = g`.  But that
25	obstruction is an artefact of the **equality**.  Read the proof of
26	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq`: the hypothesis `classDeg K L = g` is used twice, and
27	in one of the two places only `g ≤ classDeg K L` is needed —
28	
29	* to enter Riemann's inequality, via `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪) = deg W + 1 − g`, i.e. `g ≤ deg W`;
30	* to *state* the conclusion's degree, which is where the equality is genuinely consumed.
31	
32	Decoupling them gives the same theorem over a **window** of target degrees, and then the
33	reference divisor is no longer an arithmetic hypothesis: the campaign's own
34	`m • fiberWeilDivisor π` has degree `m · δ` with `1 ≤ δ` (`deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ`,
35	`one_le_windowδ`), so `g ≤ deg` is reachable at `m := g` on **every** curve, while `= g`
36	needs `δ ∣ g`.
37	
38	## The second half, and it is the one that changes another lane's plan
39	
40	At the *representability* degree `deg = g` the two conditions the chart layer treats as
41	separate are the **same condition**.  With `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` the rank anchor
42	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) reads
43	
44	  `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = deg D + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1`,
45	
46	so **`h¹ = 0` alone forces `h⁰ = 1`** for a degree-`g` divisor.  `h¹ = 0` is what coverage
47	asks for (`IsSplitWitness`, and `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s drop-free membership);
48	`h⁰ = 1` is what DAT-C GAP-2 and the chart map's injectivity ask for
49	(`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`).  `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean` says
50	effectivity and `h⁰ = 1` "are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs, not what *membership*
51	needs", which is true of the *hypotheses as written* and understates the coupling: at degree
52	`g` the membership hypothesis already delivers the injectivity hypothesis.
53	
54	That is also the sharp form of `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean`'s `hb_forces_h0_eq_one`.
55	That theorem reads its own conclusion as a defect ("`hb` at `b = g` forces **every**
56	degree-`g` divisor to have `h⁰ = 1`, false on a curve with a moving degree-`g` family") — and
57	it is right that the *universally quantified* form is too strong.  What this file adds is that
58	the pointwise form is not a defect but the χ-ledger: for one divisor, at degree `g`, `h⁰ = 1`
59	*is* `h¹ = 0`.  So the index-slack residue and the drop-freeness of coverage are two faces of
60	one identity rather than two independent findings.
61	
62	## Main declarations
63	
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg` — the window form: for **any**
65	  target degree `d` with `g ≤ d`, a class of degree `d` has an effective representative of
66	  degree `d`.  Strictly generalises `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq` (`d := g`).
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg` — the degree-zero face
68	  with the reference divisor's degree only **bounded below**, which is what removes the
69	  arithmetic hypothesis.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` — and the reference divisor at that
71	  bound **exists on every curve of the campaign bundle**, so the face above is inhabited, not
72	  relocated.  This is the declaration that discharges the retraction's "open here".
73	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_eq` — the identity: at
74	  degree `g` with `χ = 1 − g`, `h¹ = 0` forces `h⁰ = 1`.
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_eq_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` — GAP-2's
76	  uniqueness conclusion from the **coverage** hypothesis, with no `h⁰` input at all.
77	
78	## What this does NOT do
79	
80	It does not produce a chart, does not discharge `IsChartUniv`, and does not produce the
81	local-surjectivity instance.  It removes one arithmetic hypothesis from the effectivity leg
82	and identifies two chart-layer conditions at the representability degree.  The `V`-coupling
83	(I-0861, I-0869) and the `exists_factor` field are untouched and remain open.
84	-/

98	/-! ## The window form of the effective-representative theorem -/
99	
100	section Window
101	
102	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
103	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
104	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
105	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
106	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
107	
108	/-- **An effective representative at any target degree above the genus.**
109	
110	Identical in proof to `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq`, whose `classDeg K L = g` is
111	weakened to a target degree `d` with `g ≤ d`.  The Riemann-inequality entry condition
112	`1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` reads `1 ≤ d + 1 − g`, i.e. `g ≤ d` — the equality `d = g` was only ever
113	the boundary case.  The degree conjunct still comes free from `deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq`.
114	
115	Taking `d := g` recovers the original statement, which is recorded as
116	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_of_window` below. -/
117	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg (g : ℕ) (d : ℤ)
118	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ)) (hgd : (g : ℤ) ≤ d)
119	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = d) :
120	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L ∧
121	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = d := by
122	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L
123	  have hdegW : CurveDivisor.deg K W = d := by
124	    rw [← classDeg_picClass K W, hW, hL]
125	  have hentry : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) := by
126	    rw [hdegW, hχ]; omega
127	  obtain ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hentry
128	  exact ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl.trans hW, (deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq K hEcl).trans hdegW⟩
129	
130	/-- The landed `= g` statement is the `d := g` face of the window form — recorded so the
131	generalisation is visibly not a weakening. -/
132	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_of_window (g : ℕ)
133	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
134	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = (g : ℤ)) :
135	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L ∧
136	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = (g : ℤ) :=
137	  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg K g (g : ℤ) hχ le_rfl L hL
138	
139	/-- **The degree-zero face with the reference divisor only bounded below** — the shape a
140	`Pic⁰` consumer meets, with the arithmetic hypothesis removed.
141	
142	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` asks for `deg Z = g`, and its own docstring
143	retracts that as "a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open here" because `deg` is
144	residue-degree weighted.  Here `Z` need only satisfy `g ≤ deg Z`, which
145	`exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` supplies on every curve of the campaign bundle.  The
146	produced divisor has degree `deg Z` rather than `g`; that is the honest cost of the
147	weakening, and it is what the window form absorbs. -/
148	theorem exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg (g : ℕ)
149	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
150	    (Z : X.CurveDivisor) (hZ : (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Z)
151	    (L₀ : X.CechPic) (hL₀ : classDeg K L₀ = 0) :
152	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧
153	      CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L₀ * CurveDivisor.picClass K Z ∧
154	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = CurveDivisor.deg K Z := by
155	  refine exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg K g _ hχ hZ _ ?_
156	  rw [classDeg_mul, hL₀, classDeg_picClass, zero_add]
157	
158	end Window

160	/-! ## The reference divisor at that bound EXISTS — the retraction's "open here", discharged -/
161	
162	section Reference
163	
164	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
165	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
166	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
167	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
168	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
169	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
170	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
171	
172	/-- **A divisor of degree at least `d`, on any curve carrying a finite dominant map to `ℙ¹`.**
173	
174	`d` copies of the fibre divisor: `deg (d • F) = d · deg F` (`deg_nsmul'`) and `1 ≤ deg F`
175	(`one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one` read through `classDeg_fiberTwist_one`).
176	
177	**This is what makes `exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg` inhabited rather than
178	conditional, and it is the point of the whole file.**  The `= g` predecessor needed a divisor
179	of degree *exactly* `g`, which need not exist — `deg` is weighted by residue degrees, so the
180	image of `deg` is `index · ℤ`, and the campaign's own reference has `deg (m • F) = m · δ`, hence
181	`= g` requires `δ ∣ g`.  A *lower bound* asks nothing of `δ` beyond `1 ≤ δ`, which is landed.
182	
183	No rational point, no hypothesis on the index, no condition relating `g` and `δ`.  On the
184	campaign's curve the map is supplied unconditionally by `exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1`
185	(`Curve/MapToP1.lean`), whose `thetaP1` face (`Picard/ThetaShift.lean`) is what the chart layer
186	already uses. -/
187	theorem exists_reference_divisor_le_deg (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π] [IsFinite π] (d : ℕ) :
188	    ∃ Z : Y.CurveDivisor, (d : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Z := by
189	  refine ⟨d • fiberWeilDivisor π, ?_⟩
190	  have h1 : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
191	    have h := one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one (K := K) π
192	    rwa [classDeg_fiberTwist_one π] at h
193	  calc (d : ℤ) = (d : ℤ) * 1 := by ring
194	    _ ≤ (d : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) :=
195	        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 (Int.natCast_nonneg d)
196	    _ = CurveDivisor.deg K (d • fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
197	        rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul' K]
198	
199	/-- **The effectivity leg with NO arithmetic hypothesis left**: on a curve with a finite
200	dominant map to `ℙ¹`, every degree-zero class has an effective representative, of some degree
201	`≥ g` named by the statement.
202	
203	This composes `exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` with
204	`exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg`.  Compare
205	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`, which takes the reference divisor as an argument
206	and whose docstring records producing it as "a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open
207	here": here nothing is assumed about the curve beyond the package it already carries.
208	
209	What is *given up* relative to the `= g` form, stated plainly because it is the honest cost:
210	the resulting degree is `deg Z`, a multiple of `δ` at least `g`, not `g` on the nose.  A
211	consumer that genuinely needs degree exactly `g` — `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar`
212	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean`) does, through its `hdeg` field — is **not** served by
213	this, and that residue is unchanged.  What this settles is that the obstruction lives in the
214	*consumer's* degree pin, not in the curve's arithmetic. -/
215	theorem exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_toP1 (g : ℕ)
216	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
217	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π] [IsFinite π]
218	    (L₀ : Y.CechPic) (hL₀ : classDeg K L₀ = 0) :
219	    ∃ (Z : Y.CurveDivisor) (E : Y.CurveDivisor), (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Z ∧
220	      0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L₀ * CurveDivisor.picClass K Z ∧
221	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = CurveDivisor.deg K Z := by
222	  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := exists_reference_divisor_le_deg K π g
223	  obtain ⟨E, hE, hcl, hdeg⟩ :=
224	    exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg K g hχ Z hZ L₀ hL₀
225	  exact ⟨Z, E, hZ, hE, hcl, hdeg⟩
226	
227	end Reference

229	/-! ## At degree `g`, `h¹ = 0` forces `h⁰ = 1` -/

231	section RankAnchor
232	
233	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
234	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral Y]
235	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
236	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
237	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
238	
239	/-- **THE IDENTITY**: on a curve with `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`, a divisor of degree exactly `g` with
240	vanishing `H¹` has `h⁰ = 1`.
241	
242	One line from the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`: under `h¹ = 0`
243	the count is exactly `deg D + χ(𝒪)`, which at `deg D = g` is `g + (1 − g) = 1`.
244	
245	This is the coupling the chart layer treats as two conditions.  `IsSplitWitness` — hence
246	`chartLocus` membership, hence coverage — asks for `Subsingleton H¹`; DAT-C GAP-2 and the
247	chart map's injectivity ask for `h⁰ = 1`.  At the representability degree they are the same
248	ask, which is the structural reason `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean` could delete the greedy
249	drop rather than discharge it. -/
250	theorem h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_eq (g : ℕ)
251	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
252	    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ))
253	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1)) :
254	    Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K D) = 1 := by
255	  have h := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) D h1
256	  rw [hdeg, hχ] at h
257	  omega
258	
259	/-- **GAP-2's uniqueness from the COVERAGE hypothesis** — no `h⁰` input anywhere.
260	
261	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean`) is
262	DAT-C GAP-2: two effective divisors with the same class agree as soon as one of them has
263	`h⁰ = 1`.  The `h⁰ = 1` input is what `Pic0ChartPair.lean` calls the chart map's injectivity
264	obligation, and what `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean` says membership does *not* need.
265	
266	At degree `g` on a curve with `χ = 1 − g` it is not a separate input: `h¹ = 0`, which is

269	
270	So the coverage witness of `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` already carries GAP-2's uniqueness

272	`IsSplitWitness` does *not* impose and a consumer must supply.  That remaining `deg = g` pin is

274	theorem eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_eq_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (g : ℕ)
275	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
276	    {D D' : Y.CurveDivisor} (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hD' : 0 ≤ D')
277	    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ))
278	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1))
279	    (hcl : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
280	    D' = D :=
281	  Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one (K := K) hD hD' hcl
282	    (h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_eq g hχ D hdeg h1)
283

10	/-!
11	# DAT-J's Riemann–Roch half: an effective representative **of degree `g`**
12	
13	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean` splits DAT-J step 3 into a compatibility square and
14	an effectivity input `heff`, and names the spelling the effectivity half must use
15	(`exists_effective_of_picClass` / `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`,
16	which imports `Challenge.lean`).  This file discharges that half, and it is **free of the
17	divisor-representability chain**: nothing below mentions `divFunctor`, `DivFamZar`, a
18	certificate, a chart or a universal family.
19	
20	## The gap this closes, and why it was not already closed
21	
22	Every effectivity lemma in the tree stops one conjunct short of what DAT-J consumes:
23	
24	* `exists_effective_of_picClass` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:208`) and
25	  `exists_effective_of_h0_pos` (`RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean:175`) both conclude
26	  `0 ≤ E ∧ picClass E = picClass W` — **no statement about `deg E`**.
27	* `DivFamZar.exists_effective_witness` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:123`) *does*
28	  carry the degree conjunct, but only for a divisor already presented by a locally
29	  certified family, i.e. behind the whole gated carrier.
30	
31	`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:217`) demands
32	`0 ≤ D` **and** `deg D = g`, so the missing conjunct is exactly what blocked it.  The
33	conjunct is not extra work: degree is a class invariant (`deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq`), so
34	it comes for free from the class equation — which is why the shape below is a *statement*
35	gap rather than a mathematical one.
36	
37	## The degree bookkeeping, stated once
38	
39	At genus `g` the χ-normalization is `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`, so the Riemann-inequality entry
40	condition `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` reads `1 ≤ deg W + 1 − g`, i.e. `g ≤ deg W`.  A class of
41	degree **exactly** `g` therefore sits on the boundary and fires the lemma with no slack —
42	so no `fiberTwist` shift is needed, contrary to what `Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean`'s
43	docstring predicts for this brick.  (The shift is what one needs to push a class of
44	*degree zero* up to the effective range; `pic0` classes reach degree `g` by multiplying by
45	a fixed degree-`g` class, and that multiplication is the caller's business, not this
46	file's.)
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq` — over a curve with
51	  `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`, every Čech Picard class of degree `g` has an effective representative
52	  **of degree `g`**.  General: any `X`, no relative curve, no `π`.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` — **the degree-`0` face, the
54	  form the campaign uses** (the classes DAT-J holds have degree `0`).  It takes a degree-`g`
55	  reference divisor `Z` as an *argument*, so it **relocates** the hypothesis rather than
56	  discharging it — see the retraction at that declaration: a degree-`g` divisor need not exist,
57	  because `deg` is residue-degree weighted.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq` — the not-silently-stronger probe: the
59	  landed degree-free conclusion is recovered as a corollary.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_relCurve` — the same at the fibre curve
61	  `relCurve C K` of the campaign bundle, with the base normalization `hχ` transported by
62	  `chi_relCurve` and the four fibre instances installed.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_residueField` — the form DAT-J's `heff`
64	  consumes: at the residue field of a point of an arbitrary scheme `J`.
65	-/

89	/-- **An effective representative of prescribed degree.**  On a curve with
90	`χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`, a Čech Picard class `L` of degree `g` is the class of an **effective**
91	divisor `E` with `deg E = g`.
92	
93	Two landed inputs and no new mathematics: `CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq` names some
94	divisor `W` in the class, `classDeg_picClass` reads `deg W = g` off the class degree, the
95	Riemann-inequality entry condition `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` is then `1 ≤ g + (1 − g)` — an
96	equality, so the boundary case is the one that matters — and
97	`exists_effective_of_picClass` produces `E`.  The degree conjunct, which is the whole
98	reason this statement exists, is `deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq` applied to `E`'s class
99	equation: degree is a class invariant, so it transports for free.
100	
101	The genus enters only through `hχ`; there is no hypothesis on `X` beyond the curve
102	package, and in particular no `π` and no rational point. -/
103	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq (g : ℕ)
104	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
105	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = (g : ℤ)) :
106	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L ∧
107	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = (g : ℤ) := by
108	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L
109	  have hdegW : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) := by
110	    rw [← classDeg_picClass K W, hW, hL]
111	  have hentry : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) := by
112	    rw [hdegW, hχ]; omega
113	  obtain ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hentry
114	  exact ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl.trans hW,
115	    (deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq K hEcl).trans hdegW⟩

117	/-! ### The two probes this statement owes -/
118	
119	/-- **THE SATISFIABILITY PROBE, and it is the one that matters here.**  `L` is chosen by the
120	consumer but *constrained* (`classDeg K L = g`), so the failure mode is not junk-inhabitation:
121	it is that **no class of degree `g` exists**, in which case the theorem above is a vacuous
122	truth that every `sorry` census and axiom probe passes.
123	
124	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29, same session, after a fresh-context audit (`I-0799`).**  The first
125	draft of this docstring said the probe "comes back positive, and **unconditionally on the
126	curve**: the degree map hits `g`".  **That is false**, and it is false arithmetically, not
127	merely unlanded: `CurveDivisor.deg` is weighted by residue degrees
128	(`deg D = ∑ₓ Dₓ · [κ(x) : K]`, `RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean:61`), so its image is `index · ℤ` for
129	the index of the curve.  On a curve of index `3` and genus `1` over `ℚ` there is **no** divisor
130	of degree `1 = g`, and `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq` is then a vacuous truth.  The
131	campaign's own reference divisors do not escape this: `deg (m • fiberWeilDivisor π) = m · δ`
132	(`RiemannRoch/WindowLedger.lean:133`), so `= g` needs `δ ∣ g`.
133	
134	**So what this lemma does is RELOCATE the hypothesis, not discharge it** — `Z` is an argument.
135	That is still worth having, because it is the *shape* a `Pic⁰` consumer meets (the classes
136	DAT-J holds have degree `0`, not `g`, so without this face the degree-`g` statement would be
137	a theorem nobody could instantiate).  But the honest reading is conditional: **given a
138	degree-`g` divisor `Z` over the field in question**, every degree-`0` class yields an effective
139	degree-`g` divisor.  Producing `Z` is a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open here.
140	
141	Given any divisor `Z` of degree `g` (the caller's fixed reference: in the campaign
142	`m • fiberWeilDivisor π` for suitable `m`, whose degree is positive by
143	`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`), every degree-`0` class `L₀` yields the degree-`g` class
144	`L₀ · 𝒪(Z)`, and the theorem above then produces the effective degree-`g` divisor.  So the
145	hypothesis of `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq` is inhabited wherever a degree-`g`
146	divisor exists, and the shift is one `classDeg_mul`. -/
147	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero (g : ℕ)
148	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
149	    (Z : X.CurveDivisor) (hZ : CurveDivisor.deg K Z = (g : ℤ))
150	    (L₀ : X.CechPic) (hL₀ : classDeg K L₀ = 0) :
151	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧
152	      CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L₀ * CurveDivisor.picClass K Z ∧
153	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = (g : ℤ) := by
154	  refine exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq K g hχ _ ?_
155	  rw [classDeg_mul, hL₀, classDeg_picClass, hZ, zero_add]
156	
157	/-- **The not-silently-stronger probe**: the degree-`g` conclusion recovers the landed
158	degree-free statement, so nothing was smuggled into the hypotheses.  Both directions of the
159	pair "is it weaker / is it vacuous" are therefore discharged in the file itself, as
160	`I-0571`'s safeguard asks. -/
161	theorem exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq (g : ℕ)
162	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
163	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = (g : ℤ)) :
164	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L :=
165	  let ⟨E, hE, hcl, _⟩ := exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq K g hχ L hL
166	  ⟨E, hE, hcl⟩

226	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
227	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
